The CSV and TSV parsing/formatters constitute a dual pair within data interchange protocols. The parse operation transforms unstructured text into structured data, while format reverses this process. These operations are defined over finite sets of records and fields, maintaining closure under composition. Their failure modes arise from deviation from expected syntactic forms—missing quotes, incorrect delimiters, or malformed headers. In GSI, these primitives serve as evidence accumulators where each parsed row contributes to posterior belief updates about game outcomes. In GSE, they encode state transitions by converting internal event logs into standardized formats for downstream consumption. The duality manifests in their symmetric roles: parse consumes text and produces objects; format consumes objects and produces text. This symmetry enables robust error handling and validation checks at both ends of the pipeline.
